method: Compared seven hash-matched image placements with original PowerPoint-rendered slides; examined slide54.xml connector shape 687 and its endpoint shape IDs 685/677 against the complete timeline. The repeated O-GEAR logo is one image reused in three placements.

objects.evidenceText: In the tutorial's 'In-vehicle Optical Components' panel, the 'Model link' image depicts a central in-vehicle optical network model with several linked peripheral modules.
objects.reason: The distinct topology model is visible, but individual module functions and link performance cannot be identified from the photo.

objects.evidenceText: The 'POF' example photo on slide 52 shows a red-jacketed cable with its inner fiber protruding at the cut end.
objects.reason: The slide's native label ties this particular component photo to POF; no dimension or material certification is inferred.

objects.evidenceText: The component photo labeled 'Connector' on slide 52 shows a dark connector housing with two round openings and two colored leads.
objects.reason: The label and photo identify the depicted component type without implying its pinout or current qualification.

objects.evidenceText: The component photo labeled 'Header' on slide 52 shows a small metal-cased header with a dark rectangular socket.
objects.reason: The native label and photo identify the depicted component type, not a tested specification.
The O-GEAR logo decorates the slide heading; the project name and substantive program description are already native text.

objects.evidenceText: On the 2014 tutorial's projected in-vehicle Gigabit Ethernet schedule, a red dotted connector visually links the IEEE 802.3 '1 Gbps Ethernet Std.' milestone to the O-GEAR '1 Gbps Demonstration' and automotive development timeline near 2016–2017.
objects.reason: Native connector shape 687 links endpoint shapes 685 and 677 in slide54.xml; the full original slide supplies the timeline labels. This is the presentation's planned relationship, not proof those milestones occurred.
A reused O-GEAR logo appears at the upper-right of the schedule; it adds no timeline value beyond the native O-GEAR row label.
A second placement of the same O-GEAR logo decorates the support area of the schedule; milestone labels and arrows remain native slide content.
